questions.stem: At a sports club, a pennant triangle has sides 5, 5, and 8 centimeters; classify it.

options.text: Isosceles, because two sides are equal

questions.explanation: A triangle with at least two equal sides is isosceles. Here sides 5 and 5 are equal, so it is isosceles.

questions.stem: A club banner is a triangle with base 10 meters and height 4 meters; what is its area in square meters?

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A club coach proves two triangles congruent using all three side lengths; which criterion is used?

options.text: ASA, because two angles and a side match
SAS, because two sides and an angle match
SSS, because all three sides match
AAS, because two angles and nonincluded side match

questions.explanation: SSS congruence applies when all three corresponding sides are equal. SAS and ASA require angle information.

questions.stem: A club ladder leans against a wall, base 3 m from wall, length 5 m; how high does it reach?
